item.title: Flu cases show an early start to flu season
item.description:
Flu cases show an early start to flu season jenniferdhogan Mon, 09/28/2026 - 15:59

Flu season has arrived earlier than usual in Prince Edward Island, with confirmed cases and hospitalizations already reported. 

Islanders are encouraged to book their appointment to receive flu, COVID-19 or RSV vaccination to help protect themselves, their families and their communities.

"Islanders deserve access to the tools that help keep them healthy and out of hospital. That's why our government continues to make flu, COVID-19 and RSV immunization free and accessible. These programs help protect people, reduce serious illness, and ease pressure on our health-care system. I encourage Islanders to book their appointments early and take advantage of the protection available this fall."

- Health and Wellness Minister Cory Deagle

The flu and COVID-19 vaccines are available free of charge to eligible Islanders through family doctors, nurse practitioners, community pharmacies and Public Health Nursing.

PEI is also continuing its expanded RSV protection program for infants and older adults. All infants (8 months of age and younger) are eligible to receive Beyfortus® (nirsevimab), a long-acting monoclonal antibody that provides season-long protection against RSV. Adults aged 75 and older who have never received an RSV vaccine are eligible to receive a dose from Public Health Nursing. Unlike COVID and influenza, RSV does not need to be given every year.

"Immunization continues to be among the most effective ways we have to prevent serious illness from respiratory viruses," said Chief Public Health Officer Dr. Heather Morrison. "We are already seeing influenza activity in PEI, which is earlier than expected. Booking your appointment now is an important step to protect yourself and stay healthy this fall and winter."

Since introducing RSV protection programs, PEI has seen fewer cases of severe RSV illness requiring hospitalization. RSV-related hospitalizations among infants declined by approximately 90 per cent compared to the previous season, showing the value of protecting those most at risk.

To book an appointment, Islanders can:

  • Call Public Health Nursing toll-free at 1-844-975-3303
  • Visit Skip the Waiting Room – Vaccine Clinics 
  • Contact their local pharmacy, family doctor or nurse practitioner

Additionally, FluMist®, a nasal spray influenza vaccine for children aged 2 to 17, is available only through Public Health Nursing clinics.

For more information on flu, COVID-19 and RSV immunization programs, visit https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/flu or contact your health care provider.

item.title: Community meals create connection for older adults
item.description:
Community meals create connection for older adults ddgillis Mon, 09/28/2026 - 11:37

Island seniors across the province will have more opportunity to connect with one another and stay engaged in their communities through funding from the Seniors Community Meal Grants.

Forty-eight projects have been approved to host community meals for seniors. Supported by more than $150,000 in funding, these projects represent a meaningful investment in seniors’ social connection and well-being. 

"Good food tastes better with great company. These grants provide a way for older adults to come together, connect with their community, and enjoy a free meal in a welcoming setting. We are proud to support the organizations that make this possible."

-Social Development and Seniors Minister Barb Ramsay

The provincial government launched the grant program in 2024 to provide funding for organizations to host free communal meals for seniors. Applications for the recent round of funding opened in February and closed in March 2026. Successful applicants received up to $5,000 per project.

“This grant has been such a success in our community allowing us to not only host these events but bring our community together,” said chief administrative officer of the Rural Municipality of Crapaud Margaret Armsworthy. “We have dedicated volunteers and councilors who ensure these events are more than just about the food being provided. It’s also about bringing our community together.”

This program supports one of the key themes in the Seniors Action Plan 2026-2031 by enhancing access to food and social connection for seniors.

item.title: First quarter update provides early results, shows resilient economy
item.description:
First quarter update provides early results, shows resilient economy ddgillis Mon, 09/28/2026 - 11:08

The Minister of Finance Jill Burridge has released PEI’s first-quarter Fiscal and Economic Update for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. 

This information provides an early update on provincial finances and the economy as government works to manage the cost of living for Islanders and implement their prudent fiscal plan to manage expenditures and debt.

"We entered this fiscal year with a strong focus on what matters most - delivering direct affordability relief to Islanders, continuing the programs Islanders rely on, and making targeted investments in healthcare and education." 

- Finance Minister Jill Burridge. 

The current forecast for fiscal year 2026-2027 is a deficit of $440.4 million, a $30.5 million increase from the 2026-2027 operating budget tabled in April 2026. This reflects increased expenditures totaling $53.4 million in key areas including healthcare, social program funding, and the cost of diesel and heating fuel for schools due to impacts on the global supply chain.

Total revenues are forecasted to increase by $22.9 million from last spring’s operating budget and the net-debt-to-GDP ratio, a key fiscal anchor in the debt management strategy, remains at the forecast 38.1 per cent. The net debt is forecast to decrease by $2.7 million by the end of the 2026-2027 fiscal year, compared to the spring budget estimates. 

While expenditures have increased, the update shows PEI’s strong and resilient economy is improving revenues. Highlights include: 

  • Average monthly employment for the first eight months of 2026 was up 3 per cent compared to the same period in 2025.
  • Labour income grew 7.1 per cent year-to-date through June, trending above the 2026 budget forecast of 4 per cent. Average weekly earnings of $1,177 through June were up 5.3 per cent. 
  • Retail sales grew 7.1 per cent or $132 million year-to-date through June, on track to exceed the budget forecast of 3 per cent. 
  • International goods exports were up 6.7 per cent year-to-date through July, largely reflecting growth in the repair category of special transactions trade.
  • Housing starts are up 24.6 per cent year-to-date through June, with multi-unit starts accounting for the increase, and industrial construction was up 74.4 per cent.
  • Early tourism statistics show an increase in all categories of traffic to the Island as well as in overnight stays in both fixed roof accommodations and campgrounds.

“Our Island business community is vital to our economic success and businesses have demonstrated innovation and drive at every turn,” said Minister Burridge. "They create the jobs that support our families, support our communities, and supply the products the world is looking for."

The 2025-2026 Public Accounts are currently being finalized and estimates included in this update are based on the information available since the release of the 2026 spring operating budget. 

Media contact:
Janice Fogarty
Department of Finance and Affordability 
jefogarty@gov.pe.ca

                

Backgrounder 

2026-2027 First Quarter Fiscal Update

The fiscal update provides information on government’s projected revenues and expenditures as factors change throughout the year. The forecast has been compiled from information provided by management and is based on updated information and assumptions available since the budget was tabled. 

  • Current forecast for 2026-2027 indicates a deficit of $440.4 million. This represents an increase of $30.5 million compared to the deficit plan of $409.9 million outlined in the 2026-2027 Budget Estimates. 
  • Total revenues are forecasted to increase by $22.9 million from the 2026-2027 Budget Estimates. This increase is largely due to HST recoveries, and one-time Federal funding to support housing.
  • Total expenditures are forecasted to increase by $53.4 million from the 2026-2027 Budget Estimates prepared in the spring of 2026.

Supplementary Departmental Summary

  • Health PEI is forecasting an increase in expenditures of $39.2 million for their Operating Budget. Key pressures include agency staffing, wage levies and salary premiums, out-of-province contracted services, and medical supplies. These pressures are partially offset by salary vacancies/savings and delayed implementation of initiatives.
  • The Department of Social Development and Seniors is anticipating an increase in expenditures of $4.8 million compared to Budget. This is primarily driven an increase in AccessAbility Supports caseload growth, and pressures in the Seniors Hearing Aid Rebate Program, partially offset by a decrease in Social Assistance as clients transition to the AccessAbility Support Program.
  • The Department of Health and Wellness is forecasting an expenditure increase of $4.7 million, driven by the PEI Alliance for Mental Wellbeing wind-up grant commitments (offset by revenue recoveries from the Alliance) and an increase in caseload growth for the At Home Caregiver Benefit.
  • Public Schools Branch and La Commission scolaire de langue française are forecasting a combined $1.4 million increase due to high diesel and heating fuel prices driven by global supply chain disruptions.
  • The Department of Transportation, Infrastructure and Energy is forecasting a net decrease in expenditures of $1.5 million. The reduction is driven by a decrease in infrastructure grants due to delayed projects, partially offset by an increase under the Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program and in highway and bridge maintenance costs

item.title: Health PEI notifies the public of a privacy incident
item.description:
Health PEI notifies the public of a privacy incident ddgillis Mon, 09/28/2026 - 10:39

Health PEI is notifying the public of a privacy incident involving a file containing personal health information about some individuals.

During a cybersecurity incident affecting a company providing services to Health PEI, an unauthorized person obtained a copy of a Health PEI file that was created in 2011.

"Based on the information available today, we believe the risk that this information will be misused is low," said Laurae Kloschinsky, interim CEO of Health PEI. "We recognize that learning about a privacy incident involving personal health information may be concerning. We take the privacy and protection of personal health information seriously and are notifying the public to be transparent and to ensure potentially affected individuals are aware of the incident."

The affected file was created in 2011 and relates to individuals who were eligible for health care services in PEI during or before that period.

Your information may have been included in the file if you:

  • had a PEI health card number in or before 2011; or
  • were a non-resident of PEI who received health services in PEI between 2008 and 2011.

The file contained health card information, including some or all of the following information about affected individuals: first name (including middle initial or name), last name, date of birth, date of death (where applicable), gender, PEI Personal Health Number (PHN), and Medicare eligibility information.

The incident was limited to the company’s systems. Health PEI and Government of Prince Edward Island systems were not compromised or impacted, and records stored within government systems were not accessed inappropriately.

Health PEI has reported this incident to the PEI Information and Privacy Commissioner, and a file has been opened by their office. The Commissioner’s office plans to provide opportunities for affected individuals to provide input and will post updates on its website as the investigation continues: www.oipc.pe.ca. Law enforcement has also been notified.

More information, including the Public Notice and Frequently Asked Questions, is available at https://HealthPEI.ca/PrivacyBreach2026

Individuals who have questions or wish to report suspicious communication or activity may contact the Health PEI Privacy Office at: Telephone: 1-800-375-3503 (toll-free)  Email: privacybreach2026@ihis.org

item.title: Health PEI Notice of Privacy Incident – Frequently Asked Questions
item.description:
Health PEI Notice of Privacy Incident – Frequently Asked Questions gemacdonald Mon, 09/28/2026 - 09:37

Who may be affected? 

The affected Health PEI file was created in 2011 and relates to individuals who were eligible for healthcare services in PEI during or before that period.

Your information may have been included in the file if you:

  • had a PEI health care number in or before 2011; or
  • were a non-resident of PEI who received health services in PEI between 2008 and 2011.

What information was involved?

The file contained some or all of the following information about affected individuals:

  • Identifying and demographic information: first name (including middle initial or name), last name, date of birth, date of death (where applicable) and gender
  • PEI Personal Health Number (PHN)
  • Medicare eligibility information: start and end dates, eligibility code, eligibility end reason
  • Health card information: issue date, expiry date, and health card reason code

What happened?

An unauthorized person obtained a copy of a Health PEI file during a cybersecurity incident affecting a company providing services to Health PEI. Health PEI and Government of Prince Edward Island systems were not compromised or impacted and records stored within government systems were not accessed inappropriately.

What is the risk to me?

Based on the information available today, Health PEI believes the risk that the information will be misused is low. 

What should I do?

Be alert for suspicious emails, text messages, or telephone calls that request personal information or claim to relate to health coverage, government programs, or identity verification. Always verify the identity of anyone requesting personal information.

If you receive suspicious communications or notice activity that you believe may be related to this incident, please report it to Health PEI. These reports will help us monitor the situation and assess whether the risk has changed.

Individuals who wish to report suspicious communications or activity, or who have questions about this notice, may contact:

Health PEI Privacy Office
Telephone: 1-800-375-3503 (toll-free)
Email: privacybreach2026@ihis.org

Why is Health PEI notifying the public?

Health PEI is providing this notice to be transparent and to ensure that potentially affected individuals are aware of the incident.

Has this incident been reported to law enforcement or the Privacy Commissioner?

Yes. Health PEI has reported the incident to the PEI Information and Privacy Commissioner, and the Commissioner’s office has opened a file. The Commissioner’s office plans to provide opportunities for affected individuals to provide input and will post updates on its website as the investigation continues: www.oipc.pe.ca. Law enforcement has also been notified.

What is Health PEI doing in response?

Health PEI will continue to monitor the situation and take any additional steps that become appropriate based on the information available. The company is reviewing its processes and implementing measures to reduce the risk of a similar incident happening again.

Innovation PEI launches Small Business Week activity series jenniferdhogan Mon, 09/28/2026 - 09:28

Prince Edward Island’s small business community is invited to take part in a week-long series of professional development and networking activities during Small Business Week.

Small Business Week is an annual national celebration of entrepreneurship, recognizing small businesses across the nation and their direct contributions to the economy and community. Thousands of online and in-person activities across Canada are organized to celebrate the week, and everyone is invited to participate.

"Island small businesses power our economy and our communities. Supporting local matters every day, but it’s especially important right now as entrepreneurs navigate unpredictability. Small Business Week is a great reminder to make intentional choices that support the Island and Canadian economy. Our small business community is built on resilience, innovation, and grit, and Innovation PEI’s week of events is a great way to help businesses keep pace and seize opportunities in a shifting economic landscape.”

- Minister of Economic Development, Trade and Artificial Intelligence Zack Bell

This year, Innovation PEI has organized a week-long series of activities to recognize the importance of local businesses and provide learning opportunities to help Island businesses grow and succeed.

The Small Business Week activity series includes:

  • October 19, 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. - Open house and business networking event at BioFoodTech in Charlottetown
  • October 20, 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. - Lunch and Learn, Own Your Stack: AI-Built Software for Small Business presented by Coltin Handrahan of Stay Golden Custom, at Mill River Resort
  • October 21, 11:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. - PEI Export Excellent Luncheon at the Delta Prince Edward in Charlottetown
  • October 22, 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. - Lunch and Learn, Own Your Stack: AI-Built Software for Small Business presented by Coltin Handrahan of Stay Golden Custom, at Brudenell River Resort

To participate in any of the above activities, RSVP by email to innovation@gov.pe.ca.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
